papers.abstract_en: This study aimed to assess the respective associations of dietary quality and working hours with insufficient sleep and sleep disorders among US adults and to examine the associations of combined work-diet patterns. In this cross-sectional study, data were obtained from the 2007-2014 NHANES. Dietary quality was assessed using the Healthy Eating Index 2015 (HEI-2015), and working hours were measured based on self-reported weekly working hours. Four work-diet patterns were created according to dietary quality and working hours. Insufficient sleep was defined as a sleep duration of ≤ 6 h, and sleep disorders were self-reported by respondents. Weighted logistic regression was used as the primary analysis. Among the 8339 respondents, 41.1% experienced insufficient sleep and 6.9% reported sleep disorders. In the fully adjusted model, higher dietary quality was not significantly associated with insufficient sleep (OR: 0.834, 95% CI: 0.693-1.005) or sleep disorders (OR: 0.716, 95% CI: 0.506-1.014). Shorter working hours were associated with lower odds of insufficient sleep (OR: 0.828, 95% CI: 0.720-0.952), but not sleep disorders (OR: 0.848, 95% CI: 0.661-1.088). Regarding the combined work-diet patterns, individuals with a healthy diet and shorter working hours had significantly lower odds of insufficient sleep (OR: 0.697, 95% CI: 0.568-0.854) and sleep disorders (OR: 0.623, 95% CI: 0.439-0.882) after adjustment for potential confounders. In this nationally representative study, a healthy diet and shorter working hours were associated with lower odds of insufficient sleep and sleep disorders. Maintaining healthy dietary habits together with reasonable working hours may be associated with better sleep health.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: T-cell immune dysregulation contributes to persistent inflammation, tissue injury, and COPD progression, but research on T-cell dysfunction and adaptive immune remodeling remains insufficiently characterized. This study mapped publication trends, collaboration networks, the knowledge base, and emerging topics from 2006 to 2026. METHODS: Publications from January 1, 2006, to May 31, 2026, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus. Data for 2026 include publications through May 31 only and do not represent a complete calendar year. The search combined COPD-related terms, T-cell and major subset terms, and terms related to immune dysregulation or adaptive immune remodeling. After merging, deduplication, and manual screening, 327 articles and reviews were included. Bibliometric analyses and visualizations were performed using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, R, and Microsoft Excel. RESULTS: COPD-related T-cell immunity research expanded, with annual publications increasing from 4 in 2006 to 31 in 2025 and a more pronounced increase observed during 2023-2025. China, the United States, and the United Kingdom were the leading contributors. The University of São Paulo had the highest output, while Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Ningxia Medical University were prominent in institutional collaboration. Principal journals were Frontiers in Immunology, International Journal of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease, and Respiratory Research. Influential references formed a knowledge base centered on chronic inflammation, impaired immune homeostasis, airway epithelial dysfunction, and innate immune activation. Core keyword themes included inflammation, T cells, smoking, and immune response; recent directions included T-cell subset imbalance, Th17/Treg dysregulation, oxidative stress, cellular senescence, and T-cell exhaustion. CONCLUSION: Within the retrieved literature, keyword analyses identified research attention to T-cell subset imbalance, oxidative stress, senescence, and exhaustion. These patterns are influenced by the predefined search terms and database coverage and may guide further investigation of T-cell dysfunction in COPD. KEYWORDS: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; T cell; adaptive immunity; immune dysregulation; immune remodeling; bibliometrics; CiteSpace; VOSviewer.

papers.abstract_en: Balance impairment in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) reflects interacting respiratory, muscular, sensory, cognitive, and behavioral constraints. Virtual reality (VR) and exergaming offer repeated practice and feedback, but technologies and exercise content vary substantially. This narrative review integrates COPD clinical and physiological evidence with indirect motor-learning literature to propose an impairment-oriented, task-specific rehabilitation framework. Study selection was performed by one reviewer, retrieval was selective, and no formal risk-of-bias or certainty assessment was undertaken. Direct VR-specific balance evidence in stable COPD remains sparse. A principal positive balance finding comes from hospitalized patients with acute exacerbation who received additional somatosensory game exercise alongside conventional therapy; it cannot establish effectiveness in stable outpatient or home populations or isolate a VR-specific effect. Pulmonary-rehabilitation outcomes, functional mobility, direct balance outcomes, and feasibility are considered separately. The framework links observed impairments to assessments, candidate tasks, proposed mechanisms, and outcomes, with explicit distinctions between direct COPD-VR evidence, non-VR COPD evidence, indirect evidence, and hypotheses. Current findings do not establish restoration of sensory function, durable sensory reweighting, or fall prevention. Dose-matched trials with mechanism-specific measures, retention, transfer, systematic safety reporting, and patient-relevant outcomes are needed before the proposed matching rules can be validated.

papers.abstract_en: Cystic fibrosis (CF) therapeutics have changed rapidly, yet automated and scalable approaches to quantify shifts in scientific attention remain under-explored. he aim of this study was to investigate dictionary-based text mining using the bibliographic database PubMed. Publicly available PubMed CF-related records (2000-2025) were analysed using a dictionary-based pipeline applied to titles and abstracts. Term families captured three therapeutic classes and comparator concepts for major comorbidities and pregnancy. Annual term-occurrence frequencies were computed, and a restricted co-occurrence network was also conducted for 2019-2025. CFTR modulator terminology was rare before the early 2010s, increasing sharply from 2019 onwards, while antibiotic-related terminology remained consistently represented and mucoactive therapy terms varied modestly. Co-occurrence suggested potential clinical relevance. Text mining and associated data visualisations represent a novel method to summarise the evolving therapeutic landscape in CF.
